author: Google Chrome team
title: Accessibility tree is well-formed
statement: A well-formed accessibility tree helps AI agents to navigate and interact with the page.

author: Google Chrome team
title: ARD manifest is valid
statement: A valid Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) manifest, served at `/.well-known/ard.json` or linked with `rel="ard"`, lets AI agents and registries discover and verify your resources. Learn more about the ARD audit.

author: Google Chrome team
title: llms.txt follows recommendations
statement: If your llms.txt file does not follow recommendations, large language models may not be able to understand how you want your website to be crawled or used for training. The llms.txt file should be a Markdown file containing at least one H1 header. Learn more about the llms.txt audit.

author: Google Chrome team
title: `<input>` elements correctly use `autocomplete`
statement: `autocomplete` helps users submit forms quicker. To reduce user effort, consider enabling by setting the `autocomplete` attribute to a valid value. Learn more about `autocomplete` in forms
audit_check: `<input>` elements do not have correct `autocomplete` attributes

author: Google Chrome team
title: Baseline Features
statement: Lists web features used on the page and their Baseline status as of {date}. Learn more about Baseline.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Page didn't prevent back/forward cache restoration
statement: Many navigations are performed by going back to a previous page, or forwards again. The back/forward cache (bfcache) can speed up these return navigations. Learn more about the bfcache

author: Google Chrome team
title: JavaScript execution time
statement: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to reduce Javascript execution time.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoids enormous network payloads
statement: Large network payloads cost users real money and are highly correlated with long load times. Learn how to reduce payload sizes.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Minify CSS
statement: Minifying CSS files can reduce network payload sizes. Learn how to minify CSS.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Minify JavaScript
statement: Minifying JavaScript files can reduce payload sizes and script parse time. Learn how to minify JavaScript.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Reduce unused CSS
statement: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused CSS.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Reduce unused JavaScript
statement: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Mitigate clickjacking with XFO or CSP
statement: The `X-Frame-Options` (XFO) header or the `frame-ancestors` directive in the `Content-Security-Policy` (CSP) header control where a page can be embedded. These can mitigate clickjacking attacks by blocking some or all sites from embedding the page. Learn more about mitigating clickjacking.
audit_check: Mitigate clickjacking with XFO or CSP

author: Google Chrome team
title: Ensure CSP is effective against XSS attacks
statement: A strong Content Security Policy (CSP) significantly reduces the risk of cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. Learn how to use a CSP to prevent XSS
audit_check: Ensure CSP is effective against XSS attacks

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoids deprecated APIs
statement: Deprecated APIs will eventually be removed from the browser. Learn more about deprecated APIs.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Properly defines charset
statement: A character encoding declaration is required. It can be done with a `<meta>` tag in the first 1024 bytes of the HTML or in the Content-Type HTTP response header. Learn more about declaring the character encoding.
audit_check: Charset declaration is missing or occurs too late in the HTML

author: Google Chrome team
title: Page has the HTML doctype
statement: Specifying a doctype prevents the browser from switching to quirks-mode. Learn more about the doctype declaration.
audit_check: Page lacks the HTML doctype, thus triggering quirks-mode

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoids requesting the geolocation permission on page load
statement: Users are mistrustful of or confused by sites that request their location without context. Consider tying the request to a user action instead. Learn more about the geolocation permission. Also consider using the `<geolocation>` element.
audit_check: Requests the geolocation permission on page load

author: Google Chrome team
title: No issues in the `Issues` panel in Chrome Devtools
statement: Issues logged to the `Issues` panel in Chrome Devtools indicate unresolved problems. They can come from network request failures, insufficient security controls, and other browser concerns. Open up the Issues panel in Chrome DevTools for more details on each issue.
audit_check: Issues were logged in the `Issues` panel in Chrome Devtools

author: Google Chrome team
title: Detected JavaScript libraries
statement: All front-end JavaScript libraries detected on the page. Learn more about this JavaScript library detection diagnostic audit.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoids requesting the notification permission on page load
statement: Users are mistrustful of or confused by sites that request to send notifications without context. Consider tying the request to user gestures instead. Learn more about responsibly getting permission for notifications.
audit_check: Requests the notification permission on page load

author: Google Chrome team
title: Allows users to paste into input fields
statement: Preventing input pasting is a bad practice for the UX, and weakens security by blocking password managers.Learn more about user-friendly input fields.
audit_check: Prevents users from pasting into input fields

author: Google Chrome team
title: No browser errors logged to the console
statement: Errors logged to the console indicate unresolved problems. They can come from network request failures and other browser concerns. Learn more about this errors in console diagnostic audit
audit_check: Browser errors were logged to the console

author: Google Chrome team
title: Use a strong HSTS policy
statement: Deployment of the HSTS header significantly reduces the risk of downgrading HTTP connections and eavesdropping attacks. A rollout in stages, starting with a low max-age is recommended. Learn more about using a strong HSTS policy.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Displays images with correct aspect ratio
statement: Image display dimensions should match natural aspect ratio. Learn more about image aspect ratio.
audit_check: Displays images with incorrect aspect ratio

author: Google Chrome team
title: Serves images with appropriate resolution
statement: Image natural dimensions should be proportional to the display size and the pixel ratio to maximize image clarity. Learn how to provide responsive images.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Uses HTTPS
statement: All sites should be protected with HTTPS, even ones that don't handle sensitive data. This includes avoiding mixed content, where some resources are loaded over HTTP despite the initial request being served over HTTPS. HTTPS prevents intruders from tampering with or passively listening in on the communications between your app and your users, and is a prerequisite for HTTP/2 and many new web platform APIs. Learn more about HTTPS.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoid large layout shifts
statement: These are the largest layout shifts observed on the page. Each table item represents a single layout shift, and shows the element that shifted the most. Below each item are possible root causes that led to the layout shift. Some of these layout shifts may not be included in the CLS metric value due to windowing. Learn how to improve CLS

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoid long main-thread tasks
statement: Lists the longest tasks on the main thread, useful for identifying worst contributors to input delay. Learn how to avoid long main-thread tasks

author: Google Chrome team
title: Minimizes main-thread work
statement: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to minimize main-thread work

author: Google Chrome team
title: Network Round Trip Times
statement: Network round trip times (RTT) have a large impact on performance. If the RTT to an origin is high, it's an indication that servers closer to the user could improve performance. Learn more about the Round Trip Time.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Server Backend Latencies
statement: Server latencies can impact web performance. If the server latency of an origin is high, it's an indication the server is overloaded or has poor backend performance. Learn more about server response time.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoid non-composited animations
statement: Animations which are not composited can be janky and increase CLS. Learn how to avoid non-composited animations

author: Google Chrome team
title: Ensure proper origin isolation with COOP
statement: The Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) can be used to isolate the top-level window from other documents such as pop-ups. Learn more about deploying the COOP header.
audit_check: Ensure proper origin isolation with COOP

author: Google Chrome team
title: Redirects HTTP traffic to HTTPS
statement: Make sure that you redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS in order to enable secure web features for all your users. Learn more.
audit_check: Does not redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoid multiple page redirects
statement: Redirects introduce additional delays before the page can be loaded. Learn how to avoid page redirects.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Document has a valid `rel=canonical`
statement: Canonical links suggest which URL to show in search results. Learn more about canonical links.
audit_check: Document does not have a valid `rel=canonical`

author: Google Chrome team
title: Links are crawlable
statement: Search engines may use `href` attributes on links to crawl websites. Ensure that the `href` attribute of anchor elements links to an appropriate destination, so more pages of the site can be discovered. Learn how to make links crawlable

author: Google Chrome team
title: Document has a valid `hreflang`
statement: hreflang links tell search engines what version of a page they should list in search results for a given language or region. Learn more about `hreflang`.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Page has successful HTTP status code
statement: Pages with unsuccessful HTTP status codes may not be indexed properly. Learn more about HTTP status codes.
audit_check: Page has unsuccessful HTTP status code

author: Google Chrome team
title: Page isn’t blocked from indexing
statement: Search engines are unable to include your pages in search results if they don't have permission to crawl them. Learn more about crawler directives.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Links have descriptive text
statement: Descriptive link text helps search engines understand your content. Learn how to make links more accessible.
audit_check: Links do not have descriptive text

author: Google Chrome team
title: Structured data is valid
statement: Run the Structured Data Testing Tool to validate structured data. Learn more about Structured Data.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Document has a meta description
statement: Meta descriptions may be included in search results to concisely summarize page content. Learn more about the meta description.
audit_check: Document does not have a meta description

author: Google Chrome team
title: robots.txt is valid
statement: If your robots.txt file is malformed, crawlers may not be able to understand how you want your website to be crawled or indexed. Learn more about robots.txt.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Initial server response time was short
statement: Keep the server response time for the main document short because all other requests depend on it. Learn more about the Time to First Byte metric.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Avoids third-party cookies
statement: Third-party cookies may be blocked in some contexts. Learn more about preparing for third-party cookie restrictions.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Mitigate DOM-based XSS with Trusted Types
statement: The `require-trusted-types-for` directive in the `Content-Security-Policy` (CSP) header instructs user agents to control the data passed to DOM XSS sink functions. Learn more about mitigating DOM-based XSS with Trusted Types.
audit_check: Mitigate DOM-based XSS with Trusted Types

author: Google Chrome team
title: Image elements have explicit `width` and `height`
statement: Set an explicit width and height on image elements to reduce layout shifts and improve CLS. Learn how to set image dimensions
audit_check: Image elements do not have explicit `width` and `height`

author: Google Chrome team
title: User Timing marks and measures
statement: Consider instrumenting your app with the User Timing API to measure your app's real-world performance during key user experiences. Learn more about User Timing marks.

author: Google Chrome team
title: Page has valid source maps
statement: Source maps translate minified code to the original source code. This helps developers debug in production. In addition, Lighthouse is able to provide further insights. Consider deploying source maps to take advantage of these benefits. Learn more about source maps.
audit_check: Missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript

author: Google Chrome team
title: WebMCP form coverage
statement: Consider adding WebMCP annotations to the forms listed below. This helps AI agents identify and interact with these forms more reliably.

author: Google Chrome team
title: WebMCP tools registered
statement: Lists the WebMCP tools registered at the time of analysis.

author: Google Chrome team
title: WebMCP schemas are valid
statement: Valid WebMCP schemas are required for AI agents to understand and interact with tools correctly. Please fix any errors or warnings reported by the browser.

author: Google (web.dev)
title: Largest Contentful Paint (Core Web Vital) thresholds
statement: Good: <= 2.5s; Needs improvement: 2.5-4.0s; Poor: > 4.0s, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads (mobile and desktop separately).
audit_check: Is Largest Contentful Paint (Core Web Vital) within the good threshold (2.5s) at p75?
citation: Google web.dev, "Web Vitals" (2020; INP replaced FID in March 2024).

author: Google (web.dev)
title: Interaction to Next Paint (Core Web Vital) thresholds
statement: Good: <= 200ms; Needs improvement: 200-500ms; Poor: > 500ms, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads (mobile and desktop separately).
audit_check: Is Interaction to Next Paint (Core Web Vital) within the good threshold (200ms) at p75?
citation: Google web.dev, "Web Vitals" (2020; INP replaced FID in March 2024).

author: Google (web.dev)
title: Cumulative Layout Shift (Core Web Vital) thresholds
statement: Good: <= 0.1score; Needs improvement: 0.1-0.25score; Poor: > 0.25score, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads (mobile and desktop separately).
audit_check: Is Cumulative Layout Shift (Core Web Vital) within the good threshold (0.1score) at p75?
citation: Google web.dev, "Web Vitals" (2020; INP replaced FID in March 2024).

author: Google (web.dev)
title: First Contentful Paint thresholds
statement: Good: <= 1.8s; Needs improvement: 1.8-3.0s; Poor: > 3.0s, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads (mobile and desktop separately).
audit_check: Is First Contentful Paint within the good threshold (1.8s) at p75?
citation: Google web.dev, "Web Vitals" (2020; INP replaced FID in March 2024).

author: Google (web.dev)
title: Time to First Byte thresholds
statement: Good: <= 0.8s; Needs improvement: 0.8-1.8s; Poor: > 1.8s, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads (mobile and desktop separately).
audit_check: Is Time to First Byte within the good threshold (0.8s) at p75?
citation: Google web.dev, "Web Vitals" (2020; INP replaced FID in March 2024).
